cards.text: The LORD is still answering Habakkuk the prophet, who asked why God is silent while the wicked swallow up those more righteous than themselves (Habakkuk 1:13). God has just described the proud one, an arrogant man who gathers all the nations to himself like he's collecting stickers (Habakkuk 2:5). Now God says those nations will take up a taunt against him, and friend, a taunt is NOT a thank-you card.

cards.question: The nations' taunt starts with 'Woe to him who amasses what is not his.' What else does the proud one use to make himself rich?

cards.text: And the taunt has a question in it: 'How long will this go on?' Friend, I asked that exact question from the back of a junk drawer for YEARS.

cards.question: True or false: God says the proud man's creditors will forget about everything he owes them.

cards.text: His creditors suddenly arise, and he becomes their prey. That's the guy who borrowed twenty bucks from every coworker, walks into the break room, and EVERYBODY looks up at once.

cards.question: God says the remnant of the people will plunder the proud man. Why?

answers.text: Because he refused to pay tribute

cards.text: He spilled blood and brought violence on the land, the city and everyone living there. And now, here comes woe number two.

cards.question: The second woe is for the man who builds his house by ___ gain.
This man places his nest up high. What does he hope to escape up there?

cards.text: But all that climbing backfires. God says he's plotted shame for his own house by cutting off many peoples, and he's forfeited his own life doing it.

cards.question: The house won't keep quiet about how it was built. God says the ___ will cry out from the wall.

cards.text: The stones cry out from the wall, and the rafters echo it from the woodwork. Friend, every time I sneak a cookie off the cooling rack, the crumbs in my mustache tell on me EVERY single time.

cards.question: True or false: The third woe is for the man who builds a city with bloodshed.

cards.text: From the LORD of Hosts, the labor of the people only feeds the fire, and the nations wear themselves out for nothing. That's decorating a whole batch for hours and then leaving the tray in the oven ALL NIGHT.

cards.question: The labor of the people only feeds the fire. But God says something else will fill the whole earth. What is it?

answers.text: The knowledge of the LORD's glory
The songs of the freed nations
The gold of the fallen cities

cards.text: As the waters cover the sea, that's how full the earth will be. Not a little spill on the counter, friend, the WHOLE SEA.
Woe number four. This man gives his neighbors drink, pouring it from the wineskin until they're drunk.

cards.question: The fourth woe is for a man who pours drink for his neighbors until they're drunk. What does the text say he does it for?

cards.text: So God turns it around. He'll be filled with shame instead of glory, and now he's the one who has to drink and be exposed.

cards.question: The proud man poured drink for others, but now the cup in the ___ right hand will come around to him.

cards.text: Utter disgrace will cover his glory. And God isn't finished naming what this man has done.

cards.question: God tells the proud man that his violence against one place will overwhelm him. Which place?
True or false: God says the destruction of animals will terrify the proud man.

cards.text: And there's that line again: bloodshed against men and violence against the land, the city and all their dwellers. Then God asks what use an idol is, that a craftsman should carve it.

cards.question: God calls the idol a teacher of lies and says its maker trusts in his own creation. What kind of idols does he make?

cards.text: He carves it, and then he trusts it. That's me stamping a cookie and then turning around to ask the cookie for DIRECTIONS.
Woe number five is for him who says to wood, 'Awake!' or to silent stone, 'Arise!' That's me yelling 'GET UP!' at my wooden rolling pin, friend, and it has NEVER rolled itself one time.

cards.question: True or false: The idol is overlaid with gold and silver, so there is breath in it.

cards.text: Gold and silver on the outside, no breath in it at all. Then the passage turns from the idol to the LORD.

cards.question: The idol can't give guidance and has no breath. But where is the LORD?
The LORD is in His holy temple. What should all the earth do before Him?

cards.text: All the earth, silent before the LORD in His holy temple. Let that quiet sit a minute, friend, because this batch is still in the oven.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'foreign' is close enough to argue for. Card 6 and card 7 just told the baker the proud man plundered many nations, so wealth from plundered nations is 'foreign gain.' A baker could reasonably pick it.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The question sets up verse 14 as a contrast with 'But God says something else will fill the whole earth.' Habakkuk 2:14 opens with 'For,' not 'But.' The card changes how the text connects verse 13 and verse 14.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'What does the text say he does it for?' sounds like a test question about the text. It doesn't sound like Papa Dorin pausing mid-passage. It works the same way as the bad example 'According to verse 17, what swallowed Jonah?'

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Idols that glow at night' is fanciful. It doesn't match the tone of 'Idols that cannot speak' and 'Idols that never break,' so the baker can rule it out without thinking.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
